news.title: FA's Hewitt asks Infantino to release records on World Cup plan, Balogun suspension
news.lede: Soccer Football - FIFA Women's Champions Cup - Final - Arsenal v Corinthians - Emirates Stadium, London, Britain - February 1, 2026 FIFA President Gianni Infantino and Chair of the Football Association Debbie Hewitt in the stands before the match REUTERS/Ian Walton. Sept 17 - England FA chair and FIFA vice-president Debbie Hewitt has written to FIFA President Gianni Infantino seeking the release of material related to his abandoned World Cup investment plan and the lifting of U.S. striker Folarin Balogun's suspension, an FA source confirmed to Reuters on Thursday. Infantino, 56, has been under mounting pressure since unveiling a proposal to sell a commercial stake in the World Cup to private investors. The plan sparked fierce opposition, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and North America's CONCACAF among those calling for changes at the top of FIFA.

news.title: Pulisic left out of USMNT squad but Musah returns after World Cup snub
news.lede: There will be no Christian Pulisic nor Weston McKennie for the USA in the September-October international break, but Milan midfielder Yunus Musah has been called up by Mauricio Pochettino after being left out of his 2026 World Cup squad. The USMNT will be in friendly action against Peru on September 26, against Chile on September 30, Mexico on October 4 and Canada on October 7 in a bumper international break that will last a week longer than usual. Milan midfielder Musah is the only Serie A player who has been called up to Pochettino’s squad of 28 players for the September-October international break. The 23-year-old, back from a loan spell with Atalanta last season, has played a prominent role for Milan following the appointment of Ruben Amorim over the summer, and is currently being picked to start ahead of former Ballon d’Or winner Luka Modric in the Rossoneri midfield.

news.title: FA chair demands Infantino release World Cup sell-off documents
news.lede: Gianni Infantino was first elected as Fifa president in 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has been told to release all documents relating to his controversial plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup in a letter sent by Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt. Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, said that the Fifa Council should also receive a written explanation for the cancelled suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun at the World Cup. Infantino should make all documents available before the next Fifa Council meeting, which is on 15 October.
